motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: Buttons lift 2px on hover; cards lift 4px. No easing curve beyond the browser default 150ms ease.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main call-to-action button, yellow fill with a hard ink shadow.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; padding: 14px 28px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 1rem; cursor: pointer; border: 2.5px solid #1A1A1A; transition: transform 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary { background: #F7C600; color: #1A1A1A; box-shadow: 4px 4px 0 #1A1A1A; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary/low-emphasis button, transparent with an ink border.

components.name: Service Ticket
components.description: A services-grid card styled like a torn ticket stub, with a perforation dot and a colored hard shadow.
components.html:
Website Design

Custom designs that capture your personality.
components.css: .ds-ticket { background: #fff; border: 2.5px solid #1A1A1A; border-radius: 10px; padding: 26px 22px; position: relative; transform: rotate(-1deg); box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #F7C600; } .ds-ticket::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: -9px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); width: 16px; height: 16px; background: #E4E6E2; border: 2.5px solid #1A1A1A; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-ticket h3 { font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 1.15rem; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-ticket p { font-family: 'Karla', sans-serif; font-size: 0.92rem; color: #4A4A4A; }

components.name: Featured Pricing Plan
components.description: The highlighted pricing tier: full yellow fill, ink text, corner ribbon badge instead of a kicker label.
components.css: .ds-plan-feat { background: #F7C600; color: #1A1A1A; border: 2.5px solid #1A1A1A; border-radius: 10px; padding: 28px 24px; position: relative; transform: rotate(-1deg); box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #1A1A1A; } .ds-pop { position: absolute; top: -12px; right: 18px; font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; background: #1A1A1A; color: #E4E6E2; padding: 5px 12px; border-radius: 999px; transform: rotate(-4deg); } .ds-plan-feat h3 { font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', sans-serif; font-size: 1.25rem; } .ds-price { font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 1.9rem; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Form field: ink border, blue focus state, no glow ring.
components.html: <label class="ds-label" for="ds-name">Your name</label><input class="ds-input" id="ds-name" type="text" placeholder="Jane Doe">

components.description: Pill-shaped two-option switch used for the EN/FI language control.

components.name: Logo Badge
components.description: The site wordmark: an image asset (/logo.png), not a CSS-drawn text mark. Yellow-and-black rounded badge with a dog mascot, transparent corners. 40px tall in the nav, 32px in the footer.

narrative.overview: WebYello's site reads like something pulled fresh off a risograph — a small print shop's duplicator loaded with exactly two ink drums, printing slightly out of register so the two colors overlap into a third wherever they meet. The drums are now yellow and blue, chosen to match the studio's own logo mark (a yellow-and-black badge with a dog mascot); their overlap prints a warm olive-green rather than the system's earlier pink-and-blue-made-purple. This is the system's second recoloring: it first replaced an original neobrutalist yellow-and-black identity with a pink/blue duotone, then swapped pink for yellow to align with the logo — deliberately returning toward yellow, but through the same light, airy, two-drum mechanism rather than reverting to the old heavy black-on-cream neobrutalist look.
keyCharacteristics: Exactly two saturated inks (yellow, blue) plus their overlap (olive) — never a fourth first-class color
Flat, zero-blur, offset color shadows standing in for depth (stickers peeling off the page)
Alternating small rotations (±1–2°) on adjacent cards so nothing lines up too perfectly
Cool, gray-green uncoated paper as neutral ground — deliberately not cream, even with yellow leading
No kicker/eyebrow labels above any heading, anywhere
The nav/footer logo now matches the page palette natively

rules.name: The Two-Drum Rule
rules.body: The entire page is built from exactly two saturated inks plus what happens when they overlap. The drums themselves can change (they already have, twice); the rule that there are only ever two has not.

rules.name: The No-Cream Rule
rules.body: Neutral ground is a cool uncoated paper (#E4E6E2), never a warm off-white/cream — holds even now that the primary accent is warm yellow.

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No small tracked label ever sits directly above a heading as its own block. If a section needs a category word, it goes in a corner badge or nowhere — never as a kicker.

rules.name: The No-Blur Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system ever combines a shadow with blur or a soft glow.

dos: Do keep the color vocabulary to exactly yellow, blue, and their olive overlap.
Do use uncoated paper (#E4E6E2) as the neutral ground, never a warm cream.
Do give every shadow a hard, zero-blur edge.
Do put any featured/popular badge in a corner ribbon, never stacked above a heading.
Do keep body copy in Karla and every headline/label in Bricolage Grotesque.
Do use yellow-ink (#8A6D00), never full-saturation yellow, for small text.
donts: Don't add a kicker or eyebrow label above any heading, page-level or component-level.
Don't soften a shadow with blur, or combine a shadow with a glow.
Don't introduce a fourth accent color.
Don't use sharp or fully pill-shaped corners on cards.
Don't revert to the original neobrutalist yellow-and-black system just because yellow is back — the light paper ground and two-drum mechanic are what keep this airy.
